title: Gravitone — Musical Marble Machine
description: Build a marble machine out of planks, bumpers, wheels and drums, then record what it plays and export a WAV.
concept: A gravity-powered instrument workshop. Drop seven kinds of part onto a 1000x1400 board — hoppers that feed marbles, planks and funnels that steer them, bumpers that kick, spinning wheels that add energy, drum pads that thud, and a drain that recycles. Every impact plays a note tuned to the part, snapped to a scale you choose, with velocity taken from the force of the hit. Record a run and the whole performance is re-rendered offline into a downloadable WAV; the machine itself saves to localStorage, three slots, a .json file, or a share link.
features: Seven part types placed, dragged, rotated, resized and re-tuned on a live physics board
Each impact triggers a scale-quantised note with velocity from the collision speed — 4 timbres, 7 scales, any root
Five built-in machines: Cascade, Pachinko, Chandelier, Rainmaker, Carillon
Record a performance and export it as a real 16-bit WAV, re-rendered through an OfflineAudioContext
Save/share: localStorage autosave, 3 slots, .json download and import, and a compressed share link in the URL hash
PNG snapshot of the board, plus live physics sliders for gravity, bounce, flow, marble size and wheel spin

interaction.mouse: Drag parts to move them; drag the inspector sliders to rotate, resize and re-tune the selected part.
interaction.click: Tap empty board to drop a marble; tap a palette part then the board to place it; tap a part to select it.
interaction.touch: Full pointer-event parity — tap to drop, drag to move, and a bottom sheet holds the tuning and physics panels.
interaction.keyboard: Space pauses and resumes the simulation, R toggles recording, Delete removes the selected part.
